description: Shared validation cases of the AccioPass translation format (README.md, "Reglas").

The validator of this repository (scripts/validate.mjs), the loader of the API (acciopass-backend) and the overlay of the app (acciopass-frontend) must each give exactly these verdicts; the three repositories run this same file in their tests (the other two keep a copy, refreshed by their "npm run i18n:sync").
messages: validateMessage(source, candidate) for a translation -> status "ok" (with the value to use), "untranslated" (empty: the source is used, no error) or "invalid".
sourceMessages: the same for a message of the source language -> "ok" or "invalid". The app does not run these: its source language is compiled into the build.

bundles: whole repositories. Each case is "base" with "files" laid over it (an object is written as canonical JSON, a string verbatim, null removes the file). expect.validator is the verdict of the repository validator ("ok" | "error"); expect.api whether a running API takes the bundle ("accepted") or keeps the catalogue it had ("rejected"); expect.messages, when present, lists per non-source locale the full keys of project "app" that survive message by message, in source order - what the validator returns in `messages`, what the API serves when it accepts the bundle, and what the app keeps if it is ever handed those files. expect.locales, when present, lists the languages a running API offers after accepting the bundle (GET /i18n), the source first and the rest by code: a language needs a valid locale.json and at least one valid text of project "app" to be offered.

protectedKeys: the key prefixes, per project, that are never taken from a live catalogue: the app and the API only ever show those texts as compiled into their build (README.md, "Textos protegidos"). The list is owned by the code of each consumer; this copy is what their tests compare it with, so that it cannot change in one place only.
